For its tenth edition the workshop came to Amsterdam, hosted at the Tinbergen Institute, with the Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam joining Tilburg and Wageningen as co-sponsor. Nine papers covered aid fragmentation and conflict, mobile-phone monitoring in Niger, free university tuition in Ecuador, health care during Sierra Leone's Ebola outbreak, payment technology, community natural-resource management in Namibia, crop insurance bundles in Kenya, management consulting in Colombia and schooling for displaced children in Jordan.

The workshop closed with Peter Lanjouw on *How Lives Change: Palanpur, India, and Development Economics*, drawn from the long-running study of a single village in north India. That same afternoon, Jenny Aker also presented at the Tinbergen Institute's labor seminar series.

The workshop was co-sponsored by the Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam (School of Business and Economics), the Tinbergen Institute, Tilburg University (Department of Economics) and Wageningen University (Development Economics Group).

### Programme

::: {.programme}

#### Monday 3 June

- **Travers Child**, China Europe International Business School [Aid Fragmentation, Corruption, and Conflict: A Micro-Level Analysis]{.talk-title} [Discussant: Erwin Bulte]{.discussant}
- **Jenny Aker**, Tufts University [Phone Calls, Monitoring and Learning: Evidence from Niger]{.talk-title} [Discussant: Arjun Bedi]{.discussant}
- **Teresa Molina**, University of Hawai'i [The Labor Market Effects of Eliminating University Tuition in Ecuador]{.talk-title} [Discussant: Robert Sparrow]{.discussant}
- **Maarten Voors**, Wageningen University & Research [Health Care Delivery During Crises: Experimental Evidence from Sierra Leone's Ebola Outbreak]{.talk-title} [Discussant: Wendy Janssens]{.discussant}
- **Burak Uras**, Tilburg University [Payment Technology Adoption and Finance]{.talk-title} [Discussant: Wouter Zant]{.discussant}
- **Julian Jamison**, University of Exeter [The Impact of Community Natural Resource Management on Farmers' Livelihoods and Land Quality in Namibia]{.talk-title} [Discussant: Daan van Soest]{.discussant}

#### Tuesday 4 June

- **Francesco Cecchi**, Wageningen University & Research [Do Crop Insurance–Certified Seed Bundles Crowd-in Investments? Experimental Evidence from Kenya]{.talk-title} [Discussant: Marleen Dekker]{.discussant}
- **David McKenzie**, World Bank [Improving Management with Individual and Group-Based Consulting: Results from a Randomized Experiment in Colombia]{.talk-title} [Discussant: Patricio Dalton]{.discussant}
- **Jacob de Hoop**, UNICEF [Supporting the School Participation of Displaced Children in Jordan]{.talk-title} [Discussant: Menno Pradhan]{.discussant}
- [Closing lecture]{.session-label} **Peter Lanjouw**, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam [How Lives Change: Palanpur, India, and Development Economics]{.talk-title}
